issues.description: Check adds a third MANUAL state for GKE that contradicts the PR description and metadata's PASS/FAIL contract.
issues.detail: PR title and metadata.json specify PASS=single NIC, FAIL=multiple. The implementation introduces a MANUAL outcome for gke-* instances that is undocumented in the spec. Either update metadata to declare MANUAL as part of the contract or remove the GKE branch and document the false-positive in metadata Notes.

issues.description: GKE detection via name.startswith('gke-') is a brittle heuristic where an authoritative signal exists.
issues.detail: Identifying GKE-managed nodes by name prefix is a leaky string-match special case: any user can name a VM 'gke-foo' to evade the check, and legitimate GKE pools with custom prefixes will FAIL. Use the goog-gke-node label or MIG membership, ideally surfaced as an is_gke_managed field on the Instance ADT.

issues.description: Check name and CHANGELOG drift from PR title: 'single' vs 'multiple network interfaces'.
issues.detail: PR title and intent describe detecting VMs with multiple NICs, but the directory, class, CheckID, metadata, and CHANGELOG entry all use 'single_network_interface'. Pick one predicate name and align CheckID, paths, class name, and changelog so future grep and readers can tell what PASS means.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch silently emits PASS, is untested, and violates the stated postcondition.
issues.detail: When interface_count == 0 the code sets status_extended but leaves status='PASS'. A VM with zero NICs is anomalous, not compliant with a 'single NIC' contract, and no test exercises this path. Either FAIL/MANUAL the zero case explicitly with a test or remove the branch and assert it cannot occur.

issues.description: Mutable default '[]' on Pydantic network_interfaces field should use Field(default_factory=list).
issues.detail: network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = [] is fragile against Pydantic version changes and reads as a Python mutable-default footgun. Prefer Field(default_factory=list) to state the per-instance ownership invariant explicitly and match codebase style.

issues.description: Network/subnetwork URL parsing via split('/')[-1] silently truncates self-links without stating the invariant.
issues.detail: In _get_instances, network = interface.get('network','').split('/')[-1] strips project/region context, so identically named networks in different shared-VPC projects become indistinguishable. Document the 'short name only' invariant on the NetworkInterface model or retain the full self-link and derive the short name at display time.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the check works and is tested for happy paths but ships with a contract mismatch and bad-taste heuristic that should block merge. Metadata promises PASS/FAIL while the code emits a third MANUAL state for GKE, identified by a fragile name-prefix match where labels (goog-gke-node) provide an authoritative signal. The artifact's name drifts between 'single' and 'multiple' across PR title, CheckID, and changelog. The zero-NIC branch silently PASSes with no test, and minor ADT issues (mutable default, URL truncation invariant) should be tightened.
